run.change_description: lib/batcher: prevent commits racing shutdown - fixes #9687

summary.intent: Close a shutdown race in lib/batcher: a Commit could pass the closed-check, then have its request land behind Shutdown's quit marker, so the commit loop exits without ever answering it — hanging a synchronous caller forever and silently dropping an async upload.
summary.issue_fit: Full. Both PR-body commitments (serialize admission with the shutdown marker; preserve the existing shutdown error) and issue #9687's question (should admission and marker insertion be serialized so every accepted request is processed or explicitly rejected) are met by the new `admitMu` mutex, and the PR's third commitment (regression coverage for the sync-hang and async-drop cases) is met by `TestBatcherCommitRacingShutdown`.
summary.coverage: Both changed files (lib/batcher/batcher.go, lib/batcher/batcher_test.go) read in full alongside their unchanged callers (commitLoop, Shutdown, New). No coverage gaps.
check_details: Reviewer ran `go test -count=1 -race ./lib/batcher` at the reviewed head (0b87bc4788cd50664b82dd7e74c78aa2c7fc3b1c): pass, 5.3s.
Reviewer ran `go test -count=20 -race -run TestBatcherCommitRacingShutdown ./lib/batcher` at the reviewed head: pass, both `sync` and `async` subtests, 20 iterations each, no race reported.
Reviewer ran `go vet ./lib/batcher` and `go build ./lib/batcher` at the reviewed head: both clean.

Nothing in this two-file, unexported-field diff makes a full-repo build regression plausible.

observations.fact: Commit admission is now fully serialized through `admitMu`, including while a send to the buffered `b.in` channel is blocked, so concurrent `Commit` callers queue one at a time behind the mutex rather than racing into the channel as before.
observations.evidence: lib/batcher/batcher.go:266-281; the commit loop (batcher.go:205-226) keeps draining `b.in` independently, so this bounds latency without risking deadlock.

requirements.source: pr-body/"Serialize commit admission with insertion of the shutdown marker."
requirements.evidence: lib/batcher/batcher.go:50 adds `admitMu sync.Mutex`; Shutdown (batcher.go:243-252) holds it across `close(b.closed)` and the quit send, and Commit (batcher.go:267-281) holds it across its closed-check and enqueue, so the two never interleave.

requirements.source: pr-body/"Preserve the existing shutdown error for commits that arrive after shutdown starts."
requirements.evidence: lib/batcher/batcher.go:268-272 still returns `fserrors.FatalError("batcher is shutting down")` when `b.closed` is already closed at admission time; the error path and message are unchanged from the merge-base.

requirements.source: pr-body/"Add regression coverage for synchronous hangs and asynchronous dropped uploads."
requirements.evidence: lib/batcher/batcher_test.go:239-315 `TestBatcherCommitRacingShutdown` runs both `sync` and `async` modes, uses `blockingStringer` (batcher_test.go:22-34) to pin a Commit between its closed-check and enqueue while Shutdown races it, then asserts the commit completes, Shutdown returns, and the batch is actually committed. Traced against the merge-base code: without `admitMu` the commit loop would drain the quit marker first and exit, leaving the sync case blocked on `<-resp` forever and the async case's request unread, exactly reproducing both failure modes.

requirements.source: issue-9687/"Should admission and insertion of the shutdown marker be serialized so every accepted request is either processed or explicitly rejected?"
requirements.evidence: The same `admitMu` serialization (batcher.go:50,243-252,267-281) guarantees a request is enqueued strictly before the quit marker or the caller sees the explicit shutdown error; the commit loop's post-loop flush (batcher.go:227-230) then always processes any request that made it into the channel ahead of quit.
